source_reviews.independent_solution: Work transfers energy across a stated body/system boundary. In a hypothetical ideal example an external hand compressing a spring supplies energy; the spring subsequently doing work on an external block transfers energy out. A raised-object example must attribute gravitational energy to the object-Earth system. If work is the only cross-boundary transfer, input work increases and output work decreases that system's energy by the transferred magnitude. These are illustrative hypothetical examples, not observations of a source image. The source is open-ended and also asks the learner to generate and explain examples.

source_reviews.independent_solution: The selected definition attributes energy to a body or interacting-body system that can do work. Capability need not already be exercised and does not require current movement. A restrained compressed spring can do work after release. Current rest alone or merely receiving an external push supplies insufficient evidence about the body's own ability to do work; neither establishes that its energy is zero.

source_reviews.independent_solution: Work is a process of energy transfer between bodies/systems, rather than the energy possessed by a body or the rate of transfer. For the discussed system with no other transfer pathway, the magnitude of work equals the magnitude of its energy change. Incoming work supplies energy and outgoing work removes it. Other transfers prevent work alone from determining total energy change.
